abstract: BACKGROUND: Pancreatic dermoid cyst (also referred to as mature cystic teratoma) is a rare, histologically well-differentiated benign germ cell tumor. Preoperative definitive diagnosis remains challenging due to the absence of specific imaging features and reliable serum tumor markers. CASE DESCRIPTION: We present a case of a 54-year-old male patient in whom a cystic low-density lesion, measuring 3.08 cm × 2.82 cm × 2.82 cm with predominantly well-defined margins and relatively homogeneous density, was incidentally detected in the pancreatic tail during a routine physical examination. Preoperative imaging assessment indicated a cystic neoplasm; however, its benign or malignant nature could not be definitively ascertained. The initial preoperative plan under general anesthesia included laparoscopic exploration and abdominal mass resection, with a contingency plan for combined distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy. During the operation, the chief surgeon observed with the naked eye that the mass had a complete capsule and was only closely adhered to the tail of the pancreas, making it easy to resection. Therefore, the surgery was adjusted to laparoscopic pancreatic lesion resection combined with percutaneous abdominal drainage. Postoperative pathological examination confirmed it to be a cystic mature teratoma. Given the potential malignant risk associated with such lesions, regular postoperative imaging follow-up was scheduled to evaluate treatment outcomes. To date, the patient has completed over 10 months of postoperative follow-up with no evidence of recurrence. CONCLUSION: Pancreatic dermoid cysts are extremely rare, and their diagnosis depends on postoperative pathological examination. Although preoperative confirmation remains challenging, this retrospective study underscores the diagnostic difficulties in imaging-based evaluation of pancreatic cystic lesions and systematically summarizes the current research advances and conceptual framework regarding these uncommon tumors. The findings may help prevent unnecessary extensive surgical resections resulting from misdiagnosis of pancreatic primary cystic neoplasms.
abstract_ja: 背景: 膵類皮嚢腫(成熟嚢胞性奇形腫とも呼ばれる)は、組織学的に高度に分化した良性の胚細胞腫瘍であり、稀である。特異的な画像所見や信頼できる血清腫瘍マーカーがないため、術前の確定診断は困難なままである。症例: 54歳男性が、定期健診で膵尾部に偶然発見された嚢胞性低吸収病変(3.08×2.82×2.82cm)を呈した。病変は主に境界明瞭で、濃度は比較的均一であった。術前画像評価では嚢胞性腫瘍が示唆されたが、良性か悪性かは確定できなかった。全身麻酔下での術前計画は、腹腔鏡下の腹腔内探索と腫瘤切除を含み、遠位膵切除と脾摘術を併施する予備計画も立てた。術中、執刀医は肉眼的に腫瘤が完全な被膜を有し、膵尾部にのみ密着しており、切除が容易であることを観察した。そのため、手術は腹腔鏡下膵病変切除と経皮的腹腔ドレナージに変更された。術後の病理検査で、嚢胞性成熟奇形腫と確認された。この種の病変には潜在的な悪性リスクがあるため、治療成績を評価するために術後に定期的な画像フォローアップを行うこととした。現在、術後10か月以上の経過観察を終えており、再発の所見はない。結論: 膵類皮嚢腫は極めて稀であり、その診断は術後の病理検査に依存する。術前の確定は依然として困難であるが、本研究は膵嚢胞性病変の画像診断における診断上の困難を強調し、これらの稀な腫瘍に関する現在の研究の進歩と概念的枠組みを体系的にまとめている。本知見は、誤診による不必要な広範な外科的切除を防ぐことに役立つ可能性がある。
